subject: GreenLine: VPC & on-prem deployment acceptance checklist and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Mullen <sara.mullen@greenline.io>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@greenline.io
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenLine deployment inquiry — VPC / on-prem prerequisites

Hi Sofia,

Quick intro — I lead procurement & deployment gating for GreenLine. We're planning a pilot of Redwood Private in our US cloud region and need to lock down networking and security prerequisites before we sign the SOW. Before our internal kickoff on Monday we'd like: 

1) A concise checklist of network configuration items we must provision (VPC, subnets, ingress/egress rules, peering, firewall examples).
2) Typical CIDR and port recommendations for the Redwood runtime + control plane connectivity.
3) A copy of any high-level network diagram we can show our infra team.
4) SOC2 or security snapshot and a filled security questionnaire if available.

Can you share those assets and confirm a 30-minute technical sync next week? We prefer Tues or Wed morning PT.

Also looping in Security (security@greenline.io) and Procurement.

Thanks,
Sara Mullen
Senior Procurement Manager
GreenLine Logistics

(Attachment: greenline_security_questionnaire.pdf)

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Mullen <sara.mullen@greenline.io>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenLine: VPC & on-prem deployment acceptance checklist and next steps

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. I've attached a short "deployment acceptance checklist" that covers minimal required network configuration, recommended CIDR ranges, and port mappings for both Redwood Private control-plane connectors and on-prem runtime nodes. Also attached a sample network diagram you can share with your infra team.

What I'm sending now: 
- redwood_vpc_prereqs_2026-04.pdf (checklist + example cloud native security groups)
- sample-network-diagram.png (high-level: control plane, private connectors, optional NAT/egress)

Quick notes: 
- Control-plane reachability: outbound TLS to our control plane endpoints (listed on page 2) on port 443. No inbound to your infra required for hosted connectors; for on-prem we provide an agent that establishes an outbound tunnel.
- CIDR guidance: use /16 for customer VPCs that will host multiple runtime clusters; we show suggested subnets for training vs inference in the doc.
- Ports: 443 outbound for control-plane, 10250 TCP if you choose Kubernetes kubelet integration (optional), and ephemeral high ports for registry pulls depending on your registry.

Jonas (cc) will follow up with SOC2 snapshot and answers to the security questionnaire items that require product-level statements. 

I'm available for a 30-min sync Tue 28 Apr 09:30 PT or Wed 29 Apr 08:00 PT — please pick one and we'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: redwood_vpc_prereqs_2026-04.pdf, sample-network-diagram.png)

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Sara Mullen <sara.mullen@greenline.io>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenLine: VPC & on-prem deployment acceptance checklist and next steps

Sara — quick technical clarifications from infra side: 

- If GreenLine plans to run the runtime in a VPC peered to other internal services, please confirm the DNS resolution strategy (Route53 private hosted zone or conditional forwarders). We recommend private hosted zones and provide examples in the checklist PDF.
- For shared NAT egress, confirm whether you need tokenized egress (per-cluster) or a single outbound gateway. Tokenized egress helps with audit logs but adds NAT complexity.
- If you'll be using a private container registry, please share authentication method (managed identity, service principal, or static creds) so we can list precise firewall rules.

Action items for GreenLine team before sync: 
- Provide VPC CIDR & whether existing peering/VPN will be used.
- Confirm registry hostnames and whether corp proxy sits in front of internet egress.

I'll be on the call to go through the runtime requirements and a short walkthrough of the agent/tunnel behavior.

- Dev Patel
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: none)

From: Security Team <security@greenline.io>

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenLine security questionnaire and SOC2 snapshot

Thanks for the checklist. A couple of questions from our side before we proceed to the SOW: 

1) We need a current SOC2 snapshot (system boundaries + controls) and a short note on data retention defaults for log storage for the control plane.
2) Are there any cross-account IAM roles we must create, or does the solution rely solely on outbound connections from our environment?
3) Can you confirm how audit logs are collected and where they are stored (customer side vs Redwood side) and retention windows?

We'll upload our filled questionnaire once we have the SOC2 snapshot and a sample answer set for the logfile/audit items.

Regards,
GreenLine Security

(Attachment: greenline_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf)

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Security Team <security@greenline.io>, sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2026 13:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 snapshot + audit log answers for GreenLine

Hi GreenLine Security — attaching a short SOC2 snapshot and an FAQ-style doc that maps common questionnaire items to our product behaviors. Highlights: 

- SOC2: scope covers Redwood Public control plane and dedicated Private connectors. The snapshot (SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf) includes control boundary summary.
- Data retention: by default, control-plane operational logs are retained for 30 days; customers can request longer retention via support plan add-ons. Audit trails for control-plane actions are available to customers on request for Dedicated deployments; for Private we provide local audit forwarding options (see page 3 of the attached).
- Cross-account IAM roles: not required for the standard outbound agent model — the runtime establishes outbound TLS tunnels. If you opt for tightly integrated managed identity flows (registry pulls into your account), we provide sample IAM role templates.

I'll be on the sync to walk through page 2 (audit log forwarding).

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf

--
Jonas Weber
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
